what: The small edge model on the Jetson Orin Nano: pipeline smoke run, inference latency of the trained policy, and the MuJoCo physics bench
type: simulation and timing on the Jetson CPU; no arm, camera or CAN attached

host.name: orin-arm
host.board: Jetson Orin Nano, JetPack 7.2.1 / L4T 39.2.1, Ubuntu 24.04.4, 25 W mode

pipeline_quick.note: Plumbing check only. The quick model is deliberately undertrained (assist 7 of 18), the same as the quick run on the Mac.

inference_latency.checkpoint: the Mac-trained policy from edge_model run-all (19,335 parameters), copied to ~/hub-tests/edge-trained/
inference_latency.method: 2,000 single-observation numpy forward passes after 50 warm-up calls, synthetic inputs
inference_latency.note: The control loop runs at 5 Hz (200 ms per step), so the model's cost on the Jetson is negligible.

physics_bench.settings: the physics_bench defaults (elliptic friction cones); cup 3.5 cm radius x 12 cm, 50 g, friction 1.0; assumed servo gains; arm links gravity-compensated; no arm-table contact; true cup position
physics_bench.cross_platform_note: On the Mac the model missed table 7 at seed 1080 (peak 9.03 cm, docs/validation/edge-model-bench-2026-11-08.json); on the Jetson the same table passed (peak 11.99 cm). Contact physics differs slightly across CPUs, so treat single-table physics results as indicative, not exact.

not_tested: the full held-out kinematic evaluation on the Jetson (about 4.5 minutes on the Mac, so roughly half an hour here at the quick run's ratio)
any real arm, camera input or Dream reply driving the model
the GPU: the model is numpy on the CPU and does not need it
